server.py:3967-3968 (gen_workouts worker) and server.py:4062-4063 (workouts_regenerate worker) — SAME BUGGY PATTERN still present. delete_one({'id': doc['id']}) will miss cross-roster / manual / seed collisions on (user_id, date) and could reproduce the E11000 crash on those flows. server.py:2377 — existing map only queries by (user_id, roster_id). rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: _process_upload_and_generate's post-generation upsert loop queried existing workouts filtered by (user_id, roster_id) and then attempted delete_one({'id': doc['id']}) + insert_one(doc). Any pre-existing workout on the same (user_id, date) under a different roster_id (seed data, manual entries, prior rosters) was invisible to that filter, so delete_one was a no-op, and the subsequent insert_one collided with the compound unique index uniq_user_date and raised E11000. The exception propagated up and was surfaced as raw Mongo text to the frontend job endpoint. REPRODUCTION: (1) seed workout with roster_id X on date D for user U; (2) POST /api/roster/upload-and-generate with a roster whose days include D; (3) job would fail at 80% 'Generating plan' with error='E11000 duplicate key error collection: crewfit_v1.workouts index: uniq_user_date dup key: {user_id: U, date: D}'. FIX: delete_many({user_id: U, date: D}) sweeps on the actual unique key regardless of source; a per-row try/except contains any residual failure. MITIGATION VERIFIED: reran the exact scenario end-to-end — job now completes cleanly, row count is 1, no raw Mongo error surfaces.
